## Race Condition Analysis

### 1. Fast Path Read Without Lock (Lines 44-49) - CRITICAL

**The Interleaving:**
```
Goroutine A: reads c.data[key] (no lock)
Goroutine B: c.mu.Lock(); delete(c.data, key); c.mu.Unlock()
Goroutine A: accesses entry.ExpiresAt → PANIC or stale read
```

The "optimization" of reading `c.data` without holding the lock is the classic concurrent map write panic. Go maps are not safe for concurrent read/write.

### 2. Stats Updates Are Racing (Lines 47, 55, 69, 73) - HIGH

`c.stats.Hits++` and `c.stats.Misses++` are not atomic. Multiple goroutines incrementing simultaneously lose counts.

### 3. Set() Has No Lock (Lines 93-99) - CRITICAL

```
Goroutine A: c.Set("x", valueA)
Goroutine B: c.Set("x", valueB)  
Goroutine C: c.cleanup() iterating c.data
```

Pure concurrent map write chaos. Your panic reports come from here.

### 4. GetMulti() Writes to Shared Map (Lines 107-119) - CRITICAL

```go
results := make(map[string]interface{})
for _, key := range keys {
    go func(k string) {
        results[k] = value  // Multiple goroutines writing!
    }(key)
}
```

Classic concurrent map write. Also, `time.Sleep(100ms)` is not synchronization—it's prayer.

### 5. cleanup() Has No Lock (Lines 131-143) - CRITICAL

```
cleanup(): for key := range c.data { delete(c.data, key) }
Get():     c.data[key] = &CacheEntry{...}
```

Iterating and deleting without lock while others write. Panic guaranteed.

### 6. cleaning Flag Is Racing (Lines 132, 134, 142) - MEDIUM

Two cleanup calls could both see `cleaning == false` and proceed simultaneously.

### 7. waitForLoad() Reads Without Lock (Lines 83-94) - HIGH

```go

if ok && !entry.Loading   // Entry could be deleted/replaced
```

### 8. Refresh() and LoadOrStore() Unprotected (Lines 150-173) - CRITICAL

Both methods read and write `c.data` without any locking.

## The Corrected Armor

```go
type Cache struct {
    data     map[string]*CacheEntry
    mu       sync.RWMutex  // RWMutex for read-heavy workloads
    ttl      time.Duration
    loader   LoadFunc
    stats    Stats
    cleaning atomic.Bool
    loadWait map[string]*sync.Cond  // Proper wait mechanism
}

func (c *Cache) Set(key string, value interface{}) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    c.data[key] = &CacheEntry{...}
}

func (c *Cache) GetMulti(ctx context.Context, keys []string) map[string]interface{} {
    var wg sync.WaitGroup
    var mu sync.Mutex
    results := make(map[string]interface{})
    
    for _, key := range keys {
        wg.Add(1)
        go func(k string) {
            defer wg.Done()
            if v, err := c.Get(ctx, k); err == nil {
                mu.Lock()
                results[k] = v
                mu.Unlock()
            }
        }(key)
    }
    wg.Wait()
    return results
}
```

Use `atomic.AddInt64(&c.stats.Hits, 1)` for stats. Use `sync.Cond` instead of busy-wait polling. All map access must be under lock.
